name: Norway
tagline: A country shaped by water that had somewhere to be.
summary: Norway is long — its coastline, unfolded, would wrap a good way round the world — and almost everything worth seeing sits where rock meets salt water. The interior is high plateau and slow trains; the coast is fjord, ferry and fishing town. Prices are the highest in Europe and the light is the strangest: midnight sun above the Arctic Circle in June, four-hour days in December.

season.note: June and July give you the midnight sun and open mountain roads. Late September brings colour and empty trails. Late January to March is the northern lights and ski season; November is neither.

getting_around: The Bergen and Dovre railways are two of Europe's great train rides and cost less than the equivalent flight if booked early. Coastal Norway runs on ferries and express boats — treat them as public transport, not excursions. North of Trondheim, distances get serious: fly, or take the coastal ferry and give it days rather than hours.
food: Brown cheese (brunost) — caramelised whey, sliced thin, an acquired and worthwhile taste
Cured and smoked salmon, and the fresher, less-famous cod
Kanelbolle: the cinnamon bun that fuels every hike

festivals.name: Midnight sun period
festivals.where: Everywhere north of the Arctic Circle

festivals.name: Northern Lights season begins in earnest

know: Card and phone payment work everywhere, including on ferries and in mountain huts. Cash is close to useless.
Allemannsretten — the right to roam — lets you walk and camp on uncultivated land, with obligations attached: no fires in summer, no trace, 150 metres from any house.
Alcohol above 4.7% is sold only in state Vinmonopolet shops, which close early and shut on Sundays.

regions.name: Østlandet & the East
regions.summary: The populated, farmed, forested east: the capital, the big lakes, and the valleys the ski world takes seriously.

cities.name: Oslo
cities.summary: A capital that spent its oil money on architecture and then put a forest and a fjord within a tram ride of the result.
highlights: The Munch museum and the National Museum, which between them hold the versions of The Scream worth arguing about
The Fram and Kon-Tiki polar ships, kept whole in Bygdøy
Island-hopping the inner Oslofjord on a standard public ferry ticket
Nordmarka: 1,700 km of forest trail, reached by metro

experiences.name: The commuter ferry as a day out
experiences.summary: Ride the public boats to Hovedøya and Gressholmen with a swim towel and a bakery bag; it is a city transport ticket, not a cruise.

experiences.name: Waterfront architecture walk
experiences.summary: Opera roof to Munch to the library at Bjørvika — twenty years of a city deciding what it wanted to look like, in ninety minutes.

cities.name: Lillehammer
cities.summary: Olympic town on a long lake, with an open-air museum that is really a village of 200 relocated buildings.
highlights: Maihaugen: farms, a stave church and a whole timber town, walked rather than viewed
The 1994 Olympic bob track, still rideable
Cross-country trails that start where the streets end

experiences.name: Maihaugen open-air museum
experiences.summary: Two hundred buildings moved log by log from across Gudbrandsdalen; the point is the carpentry, not the costumes.

regions.name: Fjord Norway
regions.summary: The west coast: Bergen and its rain, the deep fjord arms, and the roads that only open when the snow lets them.

cities.name: Bergen
cities.summary: A hanseatic trading port wedged between seven mountains, wet 200 days a year and entirely unbothered about it.
highlights: Bryggen's leaning wooden warehouses, and the fire history that explains their gaps
The Fløibanen funicular to a mountain you can walk down in an hour
The fish market — better one street back, where the locals buy
The Bergen Railway east: seven hours across a high plateau

experiences.name: Fløyen to Ulriken ridge walk
experiences.summary: Five hours along the tops between the two cable cars, with the city on one side and nothing but bog and rock on the other.

experiences.name: Lunch at a working fish counter
experiences.summary: Skip the tourist stalls; eat where the boats deliver, standing up, whatever came in that morning.

cities.name: Flåm
cities.summary: A hamlet at the end of a fjord arm, famous for a railway that drops 865 metres in twenty kilometres.
highlights: The Flåm Railway, best taken uphill and walked or cycled back down
Nærøyfjord: a UNESCO-listed fjord arm 250 metres wide at its narrowest
Aurlandsdalen, a day-long valley walk between old summer farms

experiences.name: Ride the Rallarvegen down
experiences.summary: The old navvies' road from Myrdal, gravel all the way, downhill nearly all the way — a bike, a train ticket and a whole afternoon.

cities.name: Ålesund
cities.summary: Burned to the ground in 1904 and rebuilt, all at once, in Art Nouveau — so the whole town matches.
highlights: 418 steps up Aksla for the archipelago laid out below
The Jugendstil centre, in the old pharmacy
Day boats to Runde's puffin cliffs in early summer

experiences.name: The town that burned and matched
experiences.summary: A short walk that only works once you know the date: every façade you pass was drawn in the same three years.

regions.name: Trøndelag
regions.summary: The old seat of Norwegian kings, plus a copper town preserved by being too remote to modernise.

cities.name: Trondheim
cities.summary: A student city built around the northernmost medieval cathedral in the world, and the end of a thousand-year pilgrim path.
highlights: Nidaros Cathedral, the terminus of the St Olav Ways
The old wharves along the Nidelva, best from the Gamle Bybro
A food scene punching far above a city of 200,000

experiences.name: The cathedral, from the workshop side
experiences.summary: The stoneyard has been cutting replacement blocks continuously for a century; see that before you see the nave.

cities.name: Røros
cities.summary: A 17th-century copper-mining town of black timber houses, at -30°C for weeks at a stretch and listed by UNESCO for surviving intact.
highlights: Slaggveien: turf-roofed miners' cottages on slag heaps
The mine at Olavsgruva, 50 metres underground
Røros Martnan, the February winter market

experiences.name: Down the Olav mine
experiences.summary: Five degrees underground year-round, hard hats, and the noise a hand drill made before compressed air.

regions.name: Northern Norway
regions.summary: Above the Arctic Circle: island chains, Sámi country, whales in winter and no darkness at all in June.

cities.name: Tromsø
cities.summary: A university town at 69°N with more bars per head than anywhere else in Norway, and the aurora directly overhead.
highlights: The Arctic Cathedral and the cable car above the strait
Aurora hunting between late September and late March, inland where the sky is clearer
Whale watching off Skjervøy in November and December

experiences.name: An aurora night with a forecast, not a promise
experiences.summary: A guide who drives to clear sky — sometimes into Finland — is worth more than one who stays put; nobody can guarantee the lights, and anyone who does is selling something.

experiences.name: A Sámi reindeer herding afternoon
experiences.summary: Book with a Sámi-owned operator; the difference between a working herd and a photo backdrop is obvious within ten minutes.

cities.name: Lofoten (Svolvær)
cities.summary: Granite peaks that rise straight from the sea, red fishermen's cabins below them, and cod drying on racks every spring.
highlights: Reine and Hamnøy, the two views that put Lofoten on every screen
Ryten and Reinebringen — short, steep, and worth the calves
Sleeping in a rorbu, the cabins built for seasonal cod crews
Unstad's cold-water surf, wetsuits mandatory

experiences.name: A night in a working rorbu
experiences.summary: The old cod-fishing cabins on stilts; the good ones still smell faintly of tar and are still owned by fishing families.

experiences.name: Cold-water surf at Unstad
experiences.summary: Beach break inside the Arctic Circle, 6mm of neoprene, and a sauna afterwards that you will remember longer than the waves.
